result.rule: When the description states that one participant sends requests for proposals to several outside parties and then chooses one of them, and does not state that those parties run their own processes or act as independent participants in the interaction: Model the outreach to the outside parties and the later choice of one of them as tasks and a decision inside the lane of the participant who performs them. Do not create a pool for those outside parties, and do not add message flows to or from them, unless the description states that they act as independent participants with their own behaviour.

When the description states one sentence or step in which several distinct actions are chained on the same objects, or in which one outcome is delivered through alternative means (for example 'via X or Y'): Model each distinct action and each alternative means as its own task, in the order the description gives. If the description says one alternative is chosen, place the alternative tasks behind a decision gateway; if it does not choose, keep them as separate tasks on their own flow. Do not combine them into one task whose label lists them together.

When The description states an exclusive decision with two or more outcomes, and names a concrete action to be carried out for one of those outcomes (for example, the reviewer may accept the item or return it for changes, or a condition leads to a follow-up investigation).: Model each such named action as its own task on the outgoing branch of the exclusive gateway for that outcome, placed between the gateway and the next step. Do not leave the outcome as a bare flow, and do not omit the action when the decision is modeled. If the description also says the item is resubmitted or re-reviewed after the action, route that action's flow back to the point the description names.

When the description states one general activity performed on an object and then lists several aspects that this activity checks (for example 'to check A, B, and C'), so that each aspect is a separate check named in the description: Model each listed aspect as its own task, labelled with the check the description gives for that aspect, and connect these tasks in the order stated (or in parallel, joined by a gateway, if the description gives no order). Do not replace them with one combined task that covers all aspects. Keep the general activity only as a grouping of the aspect tasks if the description treats it as a distinct step.
